paragraphs: Katebu happoseqim (tur v"ch tyz): hattaam denahagu hannashim shello laasot melaka br"ch (rosh chodesh), mippene daaro rabbotenu za"l (prd", pereq mah), deshalosh regalim netanam hqb"h leyisrael al shem abotenu; vehaya rotzeh litten y"b rashe-chodashim lihyot moadim veraglayim gemurim, al shem y"b shibte yisrael; veachar shechateu yisrael baegel, hipsidu dabar zeh. ulekak, hannashim shello chateu baegel, hem zaku lr"ch yoter min haanashim, velaken nahagu bahem qedushsha shello laasot melaka br"ch ella raq okel- nepesh bilbad, ad kan debarayv. ubazeh yuban bs"d hakkatub biqhillat z', pasuq kch: "veishsha bekol elleh lo matzati, lebad reeh zeh matzati". parush – "bekol elleh" hu avon haegel sheameru (shemot lb, ch) "elleh eloheka yisrael" - lo matzati chete leishah, velaken "lebad reeh zeh matzati", parush, rashe-chodashim shehem mispar "zeh", asher mequddashim "p hareiyya; ukemo sheameru rabbotenu za"l (r"h k, ) al happasuq (shemot yb, b): "hachodesh hazzeh lakem rosh chodashim" - amar lo haqqabba"h lemosheh rabbenu "h: kazeh reeh veqaddesh - matzati lehannashim cheleq bo yoter min haanashim. ubazeh yuban hattaam mah sheamar hakkatub (mishle yb, d): "eshet chayil ateret balah", hoil vezaketa br"ch shehu rosh vaatara lechaddesh, kak tihyeh ateret balah. ubazeh yuban bs"d ramaz hakkatub (tehillim qych, kb): "eben maasu habbonim, hayeta lerosh pana", parush, haishsha niqret "eben" ki hi qarqa olam; kemo sheameru rabbotenu zi"li (sanhedrin ad, b); "maasu habbonim" - hachakamim shenniqraim "bonim", kemo sheameru (berakot sd, ) al tiqre "baneka" ella "boneka", vehaynu shettiqqenu kol yom beraka, lebarek "shello asani ishah"; ak beemet "hayeta lerosh pana", ki zaketa lerosh-chodesh, mah shello zaku lo haanashim.

clarification.explanation:
The authorities gave a reason for the custom of women not doing work on Rosh Chodesh (the new month): our Sages said in Pirkei DeRabbi Eliezer that the Holy One gave Israel the three Festivals for the sake of the Patriarchs, and He wished also to give the twelve new moons as complete Festivals for the sake of the twelve tribes of Israel; but when Israel sinned with the Golden Calf, they lost this. The women, who did not sin with the calf, retained a greater portion of Rosh Chodesh than the men, and therefore they observe its sanctity by not doing work, except for food preparation.

Rabbi Yosef Chaim explains that this illuminates the verse in Ecclesiastes, "and a woman among all these I have not found; only this I have found": "among all these" refers to the sin of the calf, of which it is said "these are your gods, Israel" — I found no sin among women in that; and therefore "only this I have found" refers to the new moons, which are called by the word "this" and are sanctified by sighting, as the Sages expounded on "this month shall be for you the head of months": the Holy One said to Moses, "like this, see and sanctify" — in this I found the women to have a greater share than the men. This also explains "a woman of valor is the crown of her husband" — since she merited Rosh Chodesh, which is the head and crown of the month, so she becomes the crown of her husband. It is further hinted in the verse "the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone": the woman is called a "stone" since she is "the ground of the world," as the Sages say in Sanhedrin; "the builders" are the Sages, so called from the exposition "do not read 'your sons' but 'your builders,'" and it is they who "rejected" — who instituted the blessing said daily, "who did not make me a woman"; yet in truth "it became the cornerstone" — for she merited Rosh Chodesh, which the men did not merit.
takeaways: Women customarily refrain from work on Rosh Chodesh, except for food preparation.
The reason: the new moons were meant to be complete Festivals for the tribes, and the women, who did not sin with the calf, merited them.
The scriptural hints — "only this I have found," "a woman of valor is the crown of her husband," "the stone the builders rejected" — all point to women's merit regarding Rosh Chodesh.

paragraphs: Hakkopeh leishto shettaaseh melaka br"ch, apillu bemaqom shennahagu laasot - issura qaabid. hattaam shennahagu hannashim issur melaka br"ch millebad taam hannizkar - lepi shehannashim mushrashim bammalkut, veyesh br"ch illuy lammalkut, asher lo nimtza illuy zeh betiperet shebbo mishsharashim haanashim; lekak, hannashim yihyeh lahem yom zeh leyom tob yoter min haanashim; mihu, im haish rotzeh linhog beatzmo shello laasot melaka br"ch, rashshay, utechashsheb lo litzdaqa; velekka bazeh mishshum chashash kol happatur min haddabar veosehu, niqra hedyot; veayyen "yosep ometz", siman k' v"shiyyure-beraka", siman ty"z; umizzeh tabin kamma vekamma tzerika haishsha lehizzaher biqdushshat r"ch - ki bekamma mitzvot, hannashim tepelot laanashim, veraq bazot hannashim hem iqqar yoter min haanashim.

clarification.explanation: One who forces his wife to do work on Rosh Chodesh — even in a place where the custom is to do work — transgresses a prohibition. And the reason women customarily refrain from work on Rosh Chodesh (beyond the well-known reason): because women are rooted in the sefirah of Malkhut (Kingship), and Rosh Chodesh carries an elevation for Malkhut not found in Tiferet (in which men are rooted); therefore Rosh Chodesh is a greater festive day for women than for men. Nevertheless, if a man wishes to personally refrain from work on Rosh Chodesh — he may, and it is considered an act of piety for him, with no concern of "one who is exempt from a matter yet performs it is called a fool." From this one understands how careful a woman must be regarding the sanctity of Rosh Chodesh — for in many commandments women are secondary to men, and only in this are they more primary than them.
takeaways: A woman may not be forced to do work on Rosh Chodesh (even where the custom is to work) — since women are rooted in Malkhut, and Rosh Chodesh carries an elevation for Malkhut.
Rosh Chodesh is a greater festive day for women than for men; a man who wishes to refrain from work on it may do so, and it counts as an act of piety for him.

paragraphs: Katab b"kisse-eliyyahu", siman ty"z, seip qatan d: mah shemmaqpidot hane nashe shello lehannicha kele pishtan bikbisa bizman molad hallebana, yesh lahem al mah sheyyismoku; veken katab beseper hachinnuk, bammitzvot "hachodesh hazzeh lakem", ad kan leshono. vehebio b"chesed leabraham", behaggahat hattur sham.

clarification.explanation: Some women are careful not to put linen items into the wash at the time of the new moon's birth (the molad), and they have grounds to rely upon (and this is also implied by the Sefer HaChinukh).
takeaways: Some women avoid washing linen at the time of the molad — and this has support.

paragraphs: Taanit ereb r"ch, minhag vatiqin hu; venakon sheyyitanneh qodem hammolad. veim hammolad bachatzi hayyom, yitanneh yom shellepanayv. veim chal ereb r"ch yom-shabbat, lo yitanneh beyom shishshi, mippene kebod hashshabbat, vehattaam - ki beyom shishshi yesh bo tosepet hanneshama, veen rauy lehitannot bo; velaken anshe maamad lo hayu mitannim bayyom hashshishshi; veod taam acher – shello yikkanes lashshabbat keshehu meunneh; veday lehitannot im chal ereb rosh-chodesh beyom shishshi atzmo, abal chal beshabbat - kevan deiddechi iddechi. tze ulemad mittaanit-tzibbur shechal beshabbat, shennidcha leyom chamishi. veim hammolad lel ereb r"ch, nahagu hamqubbalim shello lomar belel ereb r"ch "tiqqun-rachel", ella "tiqqun-lea" bilbad.

clarification.explanation: The fast on the eve of Rosh Chodesh (the "Minor Yom Kippur") is a custom of the pious ancients, and it is proper to fast before the molad; and if the molad falls at midday, one should fast the day before. And if the eve of Rosh Chodesh falls on the Sabbath — one does not fast on Friday out of respect for the Sabbath (the additional soul, and so as not to enter the Sabbath while fasting), since when it is postponed, it is postponed (like a public fast day that falls on the Sabbath and is postponed). And if the molad occurs on the night of the eve of Rosh Chodesh, the kabbalists were accustomed not to say "Tikkun Rachel" that night, but only "Tikkun Leah."
takeaways: The fast on the eve of Rosh Chodesh is a custom of the pious, observed before the molad; if it falls on the Sabbath, it is postponed and not moved earlier to Friday.
If the molad falls on the night of the eve of Rosh Chodesh — one says only "Tikkun Leah" that night.

paragraphs: Apillu mi sheddarko lehitannot bekol era r"ch - nakon leqabbel hattaanit bekol paam bishat mincha bayyom sheqqodem leereb r"ch; vekol shekken mi sheen darko lehitannot, shetztzarik leqabbel hattaanit bishat mincha.

clarification.explanation: Even one who regularly fasts every eve of Rosh Chodesh — it is proper to formally accept the fast each time at the Minchah service of the day before the eve of Rosh Chodesh; and all the more so one who is not accustomed to fasting, who must accept the fast at Minchah.
takeaways: The fast on the eve of Rosh Chodesh is formally accepted at the Minchah service of the preceding day.

paragraphs: Mi sheqqibbel taanit bemincha bechashebu lemachar ereb r"ch, veaach"k noda lo shettaa deen ereb r"ch lemachar, ella bayyom sheacharayv - nakon laasot hattara al qabbalato, veyachazor viqabbel hattaanit bizmanno, vekannizkar baacharonim. venireh li dehu haddin im haya hammolad beyom ereb r"ch qodem chatzot hayyom, shekkatabnu leel deen lehitannot bo bayyom, vehu lo yada veqibbel hattaanit - yaaseh hattara al qabbalato, veyitanneh achar r"ch yom echad.

clarification.explanation: One who accepted the fast at Minchah thinking that tomorrow is the eve of Rosh Chodesh, and afterward learned he was mistaken (the eve of Rosh Chodesh is a later day) — it is proper for him to have his acceptance annulled and then re-accept the fast at its proper time. The same law applies if the molad occurred on the eve of Rosh Chodesh before midday (on which one should not fast) and he did not know this and accepted the fast — he should have it annulled and fast instead one day after Rosh Chodesh.
takeaways: One who erred in accepting the fast should have the acceptance annulled and re-accept it at the correct time.

paragraphs: Tiqqenu lomar "yehi ratzon" al qabbalat r"ch beshabbat shellipne r"ch, mippene shebbeyom hashshabbat kol haam neesapim bebet-hakkeneset veshomein hahakraza. veyesh medaqdeqim lachazor lomar "yehi ratzon" hannizkar beereb r"ch beyachid, achar mincha qodem qaddish batera, uminhag nakon hu; veayyen sh"z. venahagu laamod kol haqqahal bishat hahakraza, dugmat qiddush hachodesh shehaya meummad. umah shemmebaqqeshim rachamim al chakme yisrael - mippene ki bizman qadmon hayu hachakamim meqaddeshim hachodesh "p hareiyya, umebaqqeshim kede shettachazor haatara hazzot lachakamim viqaddeshu hachodesh kebarishona.

clarification.explanation: It was instituted to say "Yehi Ratzon" for the acceptance of Rosh Chodesh on the preceding Sabbath, since then the entire congregation gathers in the synagogue and hears the announcement; some are meticulous to repeat it also on the eve of Rosh Chodesh itself, individually, after Minchah. The entire congregation is accustomed to stand during the announcement (just as the sanctification of the new month was done standing). And the reason mercy is requested for the Sages of Israel: because in ancient times the Sages sanctified the month by sighting, and one prays that this crown will return to them.
takeaways: The blessing over the new month is announced on the preceding Sabbath, said standing.
One prays for the authority to sanctify the month to return to the Sages.

paragraphs: Baamirat "mi sheasa nissim veku'" - bachorep yomar "veligshamim beittam", ubaqqayitz lo yomar ken, ella yomar "uletille beraka". gam yekavven rashe tebot "mi sheasa nissim" - shm"n, vehu b"t-b"sh shem qadosh by"t.

clarification.explanation: In saying "Mi SheAsah Nissim": in winter one says "and for rains in their season," and in summer "and for dews of blessing." One should have in mind that the initials of "Mi SheAsah Nissim" (מי שעשה נסים) spell שמ״ן ("shemen"), which by the Atbash cipher is a holy name associated with the Festival.
takeaways: "Mi SheAsah Nissim": in winter say "and for rains in their season," in summer "and for dews of blessing."
One has in mind that the initials of the phrase spell a holy name via the Atbash cipher associated with the Festival.

paragraphs: R"ch asur betaanit, vehammitanneh br"ch taanit-chalom tzarik lemetab taanit letaaniteh. vbsh"q "rab-pealim" nishalti: im hitanna taanit-chalom br"ch shechal beshabbat o byv"t shechal beshabbat, deyesh kan shette qedushshot - im day lo betaanit yom echad, o im tzarik lehitannot shene yamim keneged b' qedushshot? vehebeti reayot ledabar zeh, upilpalti bahem, veshub hebeti dibre haggaon mishbetzot zahab besiman rp"ch, seip qatan g, dipshita leh missebara denapsheh, byv"t shechal beshabbat vehitanna taanit chalom, deday lo betaanit echad letaaniteh, yeuyyan sham. veshub hebeti dibre hechakam "leqet-haqqemach" behilkot shabbat, dap t"l, ammud , dipshita leh im hitanna taanit chalom beshabbat sheyyesh bo b' qedushshot, kegon shabbat vr"ch o shabbat veyv"t, deday lo betaanit echad; ak chakam echad haya dato deyitanneh b' yamim, ayyen sham. veraiti leharab "tosepet-shabbat" shehebi dibre harab "leqet- haqqemach" hannizkar, vedato hi dela yaspiq lo taanit yom echad ledaat hassoberim detaanit-tzibbur eno oleh veku', yeuyyan sham. vaana abda hebeti bs"d reaya berura dela yoil taanit yom echad ella tzarik shene yamim, mippene shechillel b' qedushshot, vehu mishna aruka bikritot, pereq g, dap yg, ammud b: "yesh okel akila achat veku'"; umassiq sham baggemara, dap y"d (ammud ), dilolam yesh erub vehotzaa leyom hakkippurim, vehaki qatane: im hayeta shabbat vehotzio, chayyab ap mishshum shabbat umishshum yvh"k, kelomar, yitchayyeb bazeh od shene chattaot, yeayyen sham. veken katab rabbenu obadya za"l vezeh leshono: ubaggemara meparesh – im haya yom-hakkippurim shechal beshabbat vehotzio, chayyab shettayim al hahotzaa – mishshum shabbat umishshum yom-hakkippurim, sheshshenehem baim keechad, shebbeshaa sheqqadash hayyom leshabbat qodesh lyvh"k, ayyen sham; hare leka niddon zeh dame leniddon didan; ukemo deharab "masat-binyamin", siman tz"g veharab bet david, orach chayyim, siman qy"b hebi reaya lesapeq dilehon middin haqqarebban - ken yesh lehokicha lenikkavvan didan middin dikrutot hannizkar, dedame mammash - shetztzarik lehitannot shene yamim baabur shette qedushshot, vekaasher heerakti bazeh sham bs"d.

clarification.explanation:
Fasting is forbidden on Rosh Chodesh, and one who fasts a "dream fast" on it must "fast a fast for his fast" — fast an additional fast to atone for the very fast observed on the forbidden day. In his book Rav Pe'alim, Rabbi Yosef Chaim was asked: one who fasted a dream fast on a Rosh Chodesh that fell on the Sabbath, or on a Festival that fell on the Sabbath — a day carrying two sanctities — does one fast day suffice, or must he fast two days corresponding to the two sanctities? He brought proofs and analyzed them.

Among the views cited: the Gaon author of Mishbetzot Zahav concluded on his own reasoning that on a Festival falling on the Sabbath, one fast suffices for his fast; likewise the scholar author of Leket HaKemach concluded that on a Sabbath carrying two sanctities — such as Sabbath and Rosh Chodesh, or Sabbath and a Festival — one fast suffices, though one scholar held he should fast two days; and Rabbi Tosefet Shabbat cited the words of Leket HaKemach, and his own view is that one day would not suffice, according to those who hold that a public fast does not count, etc.

Rabbi Yosef Chaim himself brought clear proof that one day's fast would not suffice, but rather two days are required, since he desecrated two sanctities — from an established Mishnah in Keritot, "one who eats a single act of eating," etc.: the Gemara concludes there is a joining [eiruv] and carrying-out liability for Yom Kippur, and if it fell on the Sabbath and he carried out — he is liable for both Sabbath and Yom Kippur, two sin-offerings; and as our teacher Ovadiah explained, the two sanctities arrive as one — at the moment the day was sanctified for the Sabbath, it was also sanctified for Yom Kippur. This case is exactly parallel to ours; and just as Rabbi Mas'at Binyamin and Rabbi Beit David brought proof for their doubt from the law of the sacrificial offering, so one should prove from this law in Keritot that one must fast two days for two sanctities.
takeaways: Fasting is forbidden on Rosh Chodesh; one who fasts a dream fast on it must fast again to atone for that very fast.
A dream fast on a day of two sanctities (Sabbath + Rosh Chodesh / Festival) — Rabbi Yosef Chaim's conclusion: two fast days are required.
The proof: from tractate Keritot — one who carries out on a Yom Kippur that falls on the Sabbath is liable twice, since he desecrated two sanctities.

paragraphs: Metzuvveh leharbot bisudat r"ch; veim chal bechol, oseh bo maakol yoter mimmah sheragil bechol; veim chal beshabbat, oseh gam ken maakol yoter mimmah sheragil beshabbat. veim hu ani veen yado masseget, yosip lepachot bapperot, sheyyiqneh min peri leakelo br"ch. vegam yizzaher lekabbed seudat r"ch beshulchan, veyihyeh meseb bederek kabod. veim chal r"ch beshabbat - ita birushalmi shetztzarik laasot seudat r"ch beyom rishon; v"p shello nahagu ken - hizhir bazeh, tabo alayv beraka. vekatab rab yaabe"tz za"l besiddur: im chal r"ch beshabbat, nakon leharbot bisuda rebiit yoter mimminhago kede lehashlim bah chobat seudat r"ch.

clarification.explanation: It is a mitzvah to increase the meal on Rosh Chodesh: if it falls on a weekday — one prepares food beyond the ordinary weekday fare; and if it falls on the Sabbath — beyond the ordinary Sabbath fare. A poor person who cannot afford this should add at least a piece of fruit to eat on Rosh Chodesh. One should honor the meal at the table and recline with dignity. And if Rosh Chodesh falls on the Sabbath — according to the Jerusalem Talmud, the Rosh Chodesh meal is held on Sunday (and one who is careful about this is blessed), or one should increase the fourth meal (the one after the Sabbath's three).
takeaways: One increases the Rosh Chodesh meal (beyond the ordinary); a poor person should add at least fruit.
If it falls on the Sabbath — one completes it with a fourth meal, or on Sunday.

paragraphs: Minhag vatiqin lehadliq nerot belel r"ch; vaapillu baqqayitz sheyyoshebim al haggag vezoreach or hakkokabim baavir. vekatab harab chesed lealpayim, shehu nahag lehadliq beshabbat shiba nerot, vbyvh"k shishsha, vbyv"t chamishsha, vbr"ch arbaa, kemispar haolim leseper tora, ayyen sham. ubebetenu hamminhag lehadliq shiba - hen byvh"k, hen beyamim tobim – vbr"ch arbaa, veken bchvh"m arbaa. veotam sheddarkam lehadliq beshabbat shene nerot, yadliqu br"ch gam ken shene nerot; sheim yadliq ner echad, bammeh nikkar r"ch al yemot hachol? deha bechol name darkam lehadliq ner echad, devadday lo yeshebu bachol bachoshek; mihu, haaniyyim en lehaamis alehem shene nerot br"ch, ella yadliqu ner echad beoto ner shemmadliqim bo beshabbat; ki vadday gam haaniyyim yesh lahem nerot meyuchadim leshabbat lehadliq bahem, ubazeh nikkar kebod r"ch.

clarification.explanation: It is a custom of the pious ancients to light candles on the night of Rosh Chodesh, even in summer. Some follow different numbers of candles (Rabbi Yosef Chaim in his home: seven on Yom Kippur and the Festivals, and four on Rosh Chodesh and Chol HaMoed). And one accustomed to lighting two candles on the Sabbath should likewise light two on Rosh Chodesh (for if he lights only one, how would Rosh Chodesh be distinguished from a weekday?). The poor should light one candle — the very candle they light for the Sabbath — and by this the honor of Rosh Chodesh is distinguished.
takeaways: Candles are lit on the night of Rosh Chodesh so it is distinguished from a weekday.
One accustomed to two candles on the Sabbath lights two on Rosh Chodesh; a poor person lights one (the Sabbath candle).

paragraphs: Arbit shacharit umincha omer "yaaleh veyabo" b"retzeh"; veim lo amaro bearbit en machazirin oto - ben r"ch yom echad, ben shene yamim - mippene sheen meqaddeshin hachodesh ballayla; abal im lo ameru beshacharit ubemincha, machazirin oto. veim nizkar qodem shehitchil "modim", omer bammaqom shennizkar; veim nizkar beamero baruk atta Adonai, yesayyem "lammedeni chuqqeka"; veayyen chesed lealpayim v"kp-hachayyim". veyesh omerim dela yesayyem "lammedeni chuqqeka", ella yesayyem habberaka, veaach"k yomar "yaaleh veyabo" qodem "modim"; veayyen "chayye-adam", kelal k"g, ot k", yeuyyan sham. veim lo nizkar ad achar shehitchil "modim": im nizkar qodem shehishlim tepillato, chozer l"retzeh"; veim lo nizkar ad sheamar "yihyu leratzon imre pi" vehu mukan laaqor raglayv sheeno omer od tachanunim, hare zeh chashib keillu aqar raglayv vechozer larosh; veayyen chesed laalapim v"maamar-mareddekay" ushear acharonim. veim hu mesuppaq im hizkir im lo hizkir: ledaat mera"n b"bet yosep" tzarik lachazor, uledaat mvr"m za"l en tzarik lachazor. vehannakon sheyyachazor, vikavven bachazarato al tenay - sheim eno chayyab lachazor, tehe lindaba, vekannizkar bechesed laalapim; veayyen "shalme-chagiga", dap rk"b v"kp-hachayyim", siman l"g, ot z', yeuyyan sham. vekol shehaddin hu shetztzarik lachazor, en tzarik lomar pasuq "Adonai sepatay tiptach" paam shenit; veayyen "kap-hachayyim", ot g'.

clarification.explanation: In the evening, morning, and afternoon services, one says "Ya'aleh VeYavo" in the blessing of "Retzeh." If one did not say it in the evening service — one does not repeat it (whether Rosh Chodesh is one day or two), since the month is not sanctified at night; but if one omitted it in the morning or afternoon service — one repeats. If one remembers before beginning "Modim" — one says it at the point of remembering; if one remembers while saying "Blessed are You, Lord" — one should finish "teach me Your statutes" (Chessed LaAlafim, Kaf HaChaim); some say one should not finish this way, but rather complete the blessing and then say "Ya'aleh VeYavo" before "Modim" (Chayei Adam). If one remembers after beginning "Modim": if before completing the prayer — one returns to "Retzeh"; and if one does not remember until "Yihyu LeRatzon" and is ready to step back — it is as though he had already stepped back, and he returns to the beginning. And if in doubt whether he mentioned it — according to Maran he must repeat, and according to the Rema he need not; and it is correct to repeat conditionally (that if he is not obligated, it should count as a voluntary prayer) (Chessed LaAlafim). And whenever the law is to repeat — one need not say "Lord, open my lips" a second time.
takeaways: "Ya'aleh VeYavo" is said in all the prayers; omitted in the evening service — one does not repeat (the month is not sanctified at night); omitted in morning/afternoon — one repeats.
Remembered before "Modim" — say it there (or finish the blessing and say it before "Modim"); after "Modim" — return to "Retzeh"; after "Yihyu LeRatzon" — return to the beginning.
In doubt whether one said it — repeat conditionally (as a voluntary prayer); when repeating, one does not say "Lord, open my lips" again.

paragraphs: Im shakach "yaaleh veyabo" velo nizkar ella ad shehitpallel musap, lo yachzor achar tepillat musap, ella yitpallel mincha shettayim bishbil hattashlumin, ukemo shekkatab "shiyyure-beraka" beshem harashba" za"l, veayyen shalme chagiga.

clarification.explanation: If one forgot "Ya'aleh VeYavo" and did not remember until after praying Musaf — one does not repeat after Musaf, but rather prays the Minchah service twice, as a form of compensation.
takeaways: Remembering the omission of "Ya'aleh VeYavo" only after Musaf — one compensates by praying Minchah twice.

paragraphs: Minhag hachasidim hammitpallelim "p siddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, lomar benussach "yaaleh veyabo" "beyom rosh-chodesh hazzeh", veen omerim "hachodesh hazzeh", ki yesh kavvana bemispar "rosh" vekavvana bemispar "chodesh" belo he".

clarification.explanation: The custom of the pious who pray according to the Rashash's prayerbook is to say in the "Ya'aleh VeYavo" text "on this day of Rosh Chodesh," and not to say "this month," since there is a specific intent in the number "head" (rosh) and a specific intent in the number "month" (chodesh) without the definite article.
takeaways: The Rashash's custom: "on this day of Rosh Chodesh" (not "this month").

paragraphs: Qeriat hahallel – meummad; vaapillu lismok atzmo al hakkotel asur, ella im ken hu zaqen o chalush meod mechamat ezeh choli. veasur lehapsiq bedibbur beemtza, ak shoel bishlom adam shetztzarik linhog bo kabod, umeshib shalom lekol adam; vekol shekken demuttar laanot "amen yihyeh shemah rabba" veammanim vekayyotze. vetzarik leamero besimcha ubenachat ubeqol rinna vetoda, velo yomar bimrutza. veen omerim hallel bebet haabel, vehattaam - mishshum deomerim behallel: "lo hammetim yehallu yah", vehave keloeg larash, vekannizkar bt"z beshem "roqeach", vetaam qalush hu; ak hoil ki min haddin en chiyyub lomar hallel br"ch kelal mishshum delav qadosh hu beissur melaka, uketib: "hashshir yihyeh lakem kelel hitqaddesh chag", veameru rabbotenu za"l: layla hamquddash lechag taun shira, vesheen mequddash lechag eno taun shira; umah sheomerim hallel atta br"ch, hu mishshum minhag qadmonim shennahagu bekak, velo min haddin; velaken en gomerim bo hallel; veal-ken bebet haabel matzeu lo taam qalush; abal bachanukka, omerim hallel apillu bebet haabel, mippene dehillel bachanukka hu chiyyub min haddin, vela mashgechinan behay tama.

clarification.explanation: Hallel is recited standing, and even leaning against a wall is forbidden (except for the elderly or very weak). It is forbidden to interrupt with speech in the middle, but one may greet a person of distinction and must return anyone's greeting, and all the more so must respond to Kaddish, Kedushah, and Amens. It is said joyfully and calmly, in a voice of song, not rushed. Hallel is not said in a house of mourning. And the Hallel of Rosh Chodesh is not a strict legal obligation (since Rosh Chodesh is not sanctified by a prohibition of labor) but a custom of the ancients, and therefore it is not "completed" (the full Hallel is not said, only "half Hallel"); on Chanukah, by contrast, Hallel is said even in a house of mourning, since there it is a strict legal obligation.
takeaways: Hallel is said standing, joyfully, without interruption; it is not said in a house of mourning on Rosh Chodesh.
The Hallel of Rosh Chodesh is a custom (half Hallel), and therefore more lenient; on Chanukah it is a full obligation.

paragraphs: Bekepel happesuqim shebbesop hahallel - katab b"yosep-ometz", sop siman k', demisseper "hammanhig" umiddibre mahari"y n' giat mukach deen kopelim ella ad "hatzlicha na", veken minhag are haqqodesh yerushalayim vechebron, yeuyyan sham. vaani noheg likpol ad hassop, veken haya minhag ateret rashe harab mv"r abi zlh"h; vehattaam: dehannoheg likpol ad hassop, apillu im nomar sheen bazeh tzorek - en zeh gorea chas veshalom betosepet hakkepel; veken timtza lehariba"sh za"l, siman ql"g, vehebio beseper "yitzchaq yerannen" - beur al chibbur mahari"y n' giat za"l, behilkot hillel, seip qatan k"t, shekkatab deen lomar bazeh "halaka kerabbi mechabero, derabbi lo asar lehosip al kepalo, ella rabbi haya noheg kak verabbi elazar noheg lehosip veeno choleq, ad kan; ayyen sham. vehu haddabar asher amarti, dehammosip eno gorea. veda sheen chilluq bazeh hainyan shel hakkepel hannizkar, ben yom sheyyesh bo dillug leben yom sheen bo dillug, dibkullan yesh likpol beshaveh, ukemo shekkatabti bitshuba bsh"q "rab-pealim" bs"d.

clarification.explanation: In the doubling of the verses at the end of Hallel — some are accustomed to double only up to "Hatzlicha Na" (the custom of Jerusalem and Hebron), while Rabbi Yosef Chaim is accustomed to double to the end (his father's custom), since one who doubles to the end loses nothing even if there is no need for it. And there is no distinction in this between a day with an omission (half Hallel) and a day without — in all of them one doubles equally.
takeaways: Some double only up to "Hatzlicha Na," and some to the end (adding more loses nothing).
There is no difference in the doubling between half Hallel and full Hallel.

paragraphs: Tzarik lachlotz hattepillin qodem musap achar qaddish shel chazarat seper tora sheqqodem tepillat musap, ki ken hu minhag rabbenu haari"y za"l. veim nizdammen shehu adayin bitpillat shacharit velobesh hattepillin, veshama qedushshat "keter" mikkat acheret shemmitpallelin musap - yesalleq hattepillin mealayv ad sheyyaaneh immahem qedushshat "keter" veyannichem aach"k. veim pitom shama min hachazzan sheomer qedushshat "keter", veen lo shehut lechaletzam, kaka yaaseh: shel-rosh, yezizem mimmeqoman letzad acher; veshel-yad, yaknis rosh hattallit o hakkuttonet ben haqqetzitza uben besaro veyaaneh qedushsha; ken heela beseper "tora lishmah"; veayin mah shekkatab rab yaabe"tz za"l bassiddur.

clarification.explanation: One must remove the tefillin before Musaf, after the Kaddish following the return of the Torah scroll (the custom of the Ari). And if one is still in the morning service, wearing tefillin, and hears the Kedushah of "Keter" from another group praying Musaf — he should remove the tefillin until he answers "Keter" with them, and then put them back on. And if he has no time to remove them — he should shift the head tefillin aside from its place, and for the hand tefillin, insert the edge of the tallit or shirt between the box and his flesh, and then answer the Kedushah.
takeaways: Tefillin are removed before Musaf (the custom of the Ari).
One who hears the Musaf "Keter" Kedushah while still wearing tefillin should remove or shift them and then answer.

paragraphs: Achar shehitpallel musap lo yachzor lehannicha tepillin bo bayyom kede lilmod tora bitpillin, mippene ki harshimu nishar kol hayyom; ak bemincha yanicha tepillin; ken katab rabbenu harasha"sh za"l bannahar shalom. vahagam derabbenu hachida" za"l katab lehanicha tepillin achar musap - lo raa dibre rabbenu harasha"sh za"l.

clarification.explanation: After praying Musaf, one does not put tefillin back on that same day to study with them, since the spiritual imprint ("reshimu") remains all day; but at Minchah one does put on tefillin (following the Rashash's view). And although the Chida wrote to put on tefillin after Musaf — he had not seen the Rashash's words.
takeaways: One does not put tefillin back on after Musaf (the spiritual imprint remains); at Minchah, tefillin are put on.

paragraphs: Yomar: "zikkaron lekullam haya", veken yomar: "vesair izzim naasa beratzon". ubishnat haibbur yomar: "limchilat chete velislichat avon ulekapparat pesha". vikavven berashe tebot "rashe chodashim leammeka" – "rachel". umah shekkatub "et musap r"ch hazzeh", yesh mepaqpeqin lomar "hazzeh", ak harab "bene-yissashkar" qayyam nosach shel tebat "hazzeh" "p midrash rz"l, dilatid naqrib musapin shel kol r"ch vyv"t veshabbatot sheaberu baggalut, ulepi zeh shappir neemar "hazzeh" bekol hammusapin shel shabbat veyv"t vr"ch.

clarification.explanation: In the Musaf text one says "a remembrance for them all was it" and "a goat offering was made willingly," and in a leap year one adds "for pardon of sin, for forgiveness of iniquity, and for atonement of transgression," with intent on the initials of "heads of months for Your people" — spelling Rachel. Regarding the phrase "this Musaf of Rosh Chodesh" — some question the word "this," but others upheld it (based on the midrash that in the future we will offer the Musaf sacrifices of all the new moons and Festivals that passed during the exile).
takeaways: In the Musaf text, the initials of a certain phrase are intended to spell "Rachel."
In a leap year, one adds "for pardon of sin, for forgiveness of iniquity, and for atonement of transgression."

paragraphs: Metzuvveh lehishtaddel laalot leseper tora br"ch, vehammashlim hu yoter meshubbach; veken darko shel ateret rashe harab mv"r abi zlh"h laalot bekol r"ch, choq velo yaabor; veim r"ch shene yamim, haya oleh bishnehem, ak haya omer, haaliyya shel yom sheni dr"ch hi yoter meulla min aliyya deyom rishon; vahagam shello meporash dabar zeh bedibre rabbenu haari"y za"l baadipot leyom sheni baaliyya al yom rishon, mikkol maqom haki mistabbera bevadday.

clarification.explanation: It is a mitzvah to strive to receive an aliyah to the Torah on Rosh Chodesh, and the one who completes the reading (the last aliyah) is more praiseworthy. It was the custom of Rabbi Yosef Chaim's father to receive an aliyah every Rosh Chodesh without skipping; and if Rosh Chodesh was two days, he received an aliyah on both, and he said that the aliyah of the second day is superior to that of the first day.
takeaways: One should strive to receive a Torah aliyah on Rosh Chodesh (the completing aliyah is most praiseworthy).
On a two-day Rosh Chodesh, the aliyah of the second day is superior to that of the first.

paragraphs: Mazkirin "yaaleh veyabo" bebirkat hammazon; veim lo amaro, en machazirin oto; veim nizkar qodem shehitchil "hattob vehammetib", omer: "baruk shennatan r"ch leammo yisrael lezikkaron". vekatab beseper chasidim veen laqutz hatztzippareniyyim br"ch, yeuyyan sham. mihu, vadday im hem arukkim deodepim al habbasar, tzarik laqutz otam gam br"ch.

clarification.explanation: "Ya'aleh VeYavo" is mentioned in the Grace After Meals; if one forgot it — one does not repeat. And if one remembers before beginning "HaTov VehaMeitiv" — one says "Blessed is He who gave new moons to His people Israel as a remembrance." The Sefer Chassidim wrote that one should not trim fingernails on Rosh Chodesh; but if they are long and protrude beyond the flesh — one may trim them even on Rosh Chodesh.
takeaways: "Ya'aleh VeYavo" is mentioned in the Grace After Meals (if forgotten, one does not repeat, but there is a special formula).
Fingernails are not trimmed on Rosh Chodesh, unless they protrude beyond the flesh.

paragraphs: Birkat hallebana yomar besimcha ubenachat vesapa berura, ki hu kimqabbel pene shekina; velaken chasidim veanshe-maaseh nohagim litbol bayyom qodem birkat hallebana, vehu minhag yapeh, biprat im eno tahor mittashmish-hammitta. veim hu betaanit, tob sheyyitam ezeh dabar qodem birkat hallebana. velo yebarek ad sheyyihyeh vadday layla vetihyeh zerichatah nikkeret al gabbe qarqa.

clarification.explanation: The blessing of the moon (Kiddush Levanah) should be said joyfully, calmly, and in a clear voice, as one receiving the Divine Presence; therefore pious and devout individuals immerse before the blessing of the moon (especially if not ritually pure from marital relations). And if one is fasting — it is good to taste something beforehand. One should not recite the blessing until it is certainly night, and the moonlight is discernible on the ground.
takeaways: The blessing of the moon is said joyfully and with intent, as one receiving the Divine Presence.
Only at certain nightfall, when its light is discernible on the ground.

paragraphs: Tzarik sheyyaabru aleha shiba yamim shelemim meet hammolad, keneged keter chakema bina daat chesed gebura tiperet. veim anan apillu daq aleha, lo yebarek. vekol hallayla zemannah hu, apillu achar chatzot. vetzarik leyashsher raglayv kitpillat y"ch. ukesheyyomar "ki ereh shameka maaseh etzbeoteka veku'" yireh otah veyistakkel bah, abal kesheyyatchil lebarek lo yireh bah od kelal.

clarification.explanation: Seven full days must pass from the molad before blessing the moon (corresponding to the seven [lower] sefirot). And if there is any cloud over it, even a thin one — one should not recite the blessing. Its time extends all night, even after midnight. One straightens one's feet as in the Amidah prayer. When saying "for I shall see Your heavens, the work of Your fingers" — one should look and gaze at the moon, but once beginning the blessing itself — one should no longer look at it at all.
takeaways: The blessing is said after seven full days from the molad, with no cloud, standing upright.
One looks at the moon before the blessing, but once the blessing itself begins, one no longer looks at it.

paragraphs: Suma lo yebarek, mishshum deikka pelugta bazeh vesapeq berakot lehaqel; ella yaamod etzel hachazzan hambarek vayyomer lo sheyyekavven alayv, veyetze yede choba bishmia. veharoeh "y batte-enayim (mishsheqqepayim) – yebarek, "p shello yakol lirot belo batte-enayim. vetzarik lebarek tachat avir haraqia velo tachat haggag; veraq im i epshar lo bekak mishshum shehu choleh o sibba acheret, yebarek tachat haggag; vetob laamod al maqom chalul mittachtayv im epshar lo bekak.

clarification.explanation: A blind person does not recite the blessing of the moon himself (due to a dispute and the rule of leniency in matters of blessings), but should stand near the cantor reciting the blessing and tell him to have him in mind, fulfilling the obligation by listening. One who sees through eyeglasses — does recite the blessing, even though he cannot see without them. The blessing is said under the open sky, not under a roof (unless impossible due to illness or the like), and it is good to stand over a hollow spot beneath, if possible.
takeaways: A blind person does not recite the blessing himself but fulfills it by listening to the cantor; one who sees with eyeglasses does recite it.
The blessing is said under the open sky, not under a roof.

paragraphs: Kesheomer "keshem sheanachnu meraqqedim" yedalleg shelosha dillugim davqa, veken bepaam sheniyya veken bashshelishit; veyesh sod baddabar keneged aliyyot hassepirot shemmekavvenim bahem atta. upoh irenu bagdad nohagim ledalleg haddillugim beameram "siman tob tehi lanu", vaana abda oseh keminhag hair; ak kesheani omer "keshem sheanachnu meraqqedim" adalleg od shelosha dillugim, veken ani moreh laacherim. uminhagenu poh ledalleg shelosha dillugim kesheomerim "david melek yisrael chay veqayyam".

clarification.explanation: When saying "just as we dance," one should jump specifically three times, and likewise the second and third times (there is a mystical significance corresponding to the ascents of the sefirot). In Baghdad the custom was to jump while saying "may it be a good sign for us"; Rabbi Yosef Chaim follows the city's custom, and additionally jumps three times also when saying "just as we dance," and so instructs others. They were likewise accustomed to jump three times when saying "David, King of Israel, lives and endures."
takeaways: One jumps three times at "just as we dance" (and likewise at "David, King of Israel").

paragraphs: Lo yomar "sheap hem" ella yomar "sheggam hem"; veyomar "tehi lanu" velo "tihyeh"; veim mebarek beyachid, yomar "keshem sheani meraqqed". vekatub beketer malkut ketibat yad: beamero "david melek yisrael" yekavven "david" male beot yo"d, veken ani noheg. veiqqar hannosach hu lomar "baruk yotzerek veku'" al seder otiyyot "yaaqob"; veal daat hassod: yotzerek, keneged yetzira; osek – asiyya; qoneka – atzilut; boreek - beria. vekatabti bsh"q "mqbtzl" bs"d, deseder zeh hu keneged tzerup "vehaya" asher by"b tzerupe shem havaya"h, vezeh hatztzerup sholet betishre shebbo nibra haolam, vehitchil adam harishon limnot lallebana; velaken omerim lebassop "shalom", al derek "vehaya maaseh hatztzedaqa shalom". od amarti: rashe tebot "yotzerek, osek, qoneka, boreek" - qp"b, keminyan shiba hvyv"t, veyadua deen meqaddeshin hallebana ad achar shiba shelemim, shehem keneged shiba sepirot: kchb"t chg"t(keter chakema bina daat chesed gebura tiperet); veyadua, kol sepira yesh bah shem havaya"h. veha deen mebarekin beshabbat vyv"t - ayyen "pachad-yitzchaq" za"l shekkatab kamma teamim vekullam chalushim; veraq taam zeh adip: mippene shebbebirkat hallebana tzarik leorer bah simcha, ubeshabbat vyv"t belav haki ikka simcha, veeno nikkar kebod hallebana bazeh. vbsh"q "mqbtzl" katabti: mippene shetztzarik leqallel et oyebim bappasuq "tippol alehem emata veku'", veen meqallelin beshabbat vyv"t, deen macharimin bahem; veod katabti sham teamim.

clarification.explanation: In the blessing of the moon: one should say "she'gam hem" ("that they too") and not "she'af hem"; one should say "tehi lanu" ("may it be for us") and not "tihyeh"; and one praying alone should say "just as I dance." And in "Keter Malchut": when saying "David, King of Israel," one should have in mind "David" spelled fully with a yud (and so the Ben Ish Chai is accustomed). The main text "Blessed is your Molder..." follows the order of the letters of "Jacob"; and mystically: "your Molder" corresponds to Yetzirah (Formation), "your Maker" to Asiyah (Action), "your Owner" to Atzilut (Emanation), "your Creator" to Beriah (Creation). The Ben Ish Chai (in Miqabtzeel) writes that this order corresponds to the combination "VeHayah" (one of the twelve combinations of the Tetragrammaton) that governs the month of Tishrei (in which the world was created and Adam began counting by the moon), and therefore one concludes with "Shalom" ("and the work of righteousness shall be peace"). Further: the initials of "your Molder, your Maker, your Owner, your Creator" total 182, corresponding to the numerical value of the seven divine Names — since the moon is not sanctified until after seven full days, corresponding to the seven sefirot (each containing the Name). And the reason the blessing is not said on the Sabbath or a Festival — the preferred reason: the blessing of the moon requires an awakening of joy, whereas on the Sabbath and Festivals there is already inherent joy and the honor of the moon is not distinguished; and further (Miqabtzeel): since one must curse the enemies ("may dread and fear fall upon them"), and one does not curse on the Sabbath or a Festival.
takeaways: Precise wording in the blessing of the moon: "she'gam hem" (not "she'af hem"), "tehi lanu," and alone: "just as I dance"; intending "David" spelled fully, and the text "your Molder, your Maker, your Owner, your Creator" corresponding to Formation-Action-Emanation-Creation.

The blessing is not said until after seven full days (corresponding to the seven sefirot/divine Names); and not on the Sabbath or Festivals, since it requires an awakening of joy (already present then) and requires cursing the enemies (not done then).

paragraphs: Achar haddillugim yomar shiba peamim pasuq: "leb tahor bera li elohim, verucha nakon chaddesh beqirbi", keneged: kechabba"d chg"t(keter chakema bina daat chesed gebura tiperet), veaach"k "shir lammaalot essa enay el heharim veku'", umizmor "halluyah hallu el beqadesho", vekannizkar kol zeh besiddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l. vekatub beseper keter malkut ketibat yad, derauy lomar atta pasuq: "vehaya or hallebana keor hachamma, veor hachamma yihyeh shibatayim keor shibat hayyamim, beyom chabosh Adonai et sheber ammo umachatz makkato yirpa", ad kan debarayv; vehamchabber lo beer taam zeh, vaana abda matzati taam nakon, ki raiti beseper "mebo-shearim" besopo, kavvanot al nosach birkat hallebana, vekatab sham shezzeh hu sod happasuq: "vehaya or hallebana keor hachamma", ubeer oto kullo besodot asher rimmezam benosach habberaka, vekannizkar sham, dap qk"h, ammud b, vqk"v, ammud , ayyen sham; veken raiti debarim ellu beseper "peri- etz-chayyim", depus dvbrvnh, bedap q"ch, ammud d, yeuyyan sham. veayyen bekavvanat siddur rabbenu harasha"sh za"l, ulepi zeh nimtza amirat pasuq zeh atta, dabar beitto mah tob.

clarification.explanation: After the jumps, one says seven times the verse "Create in me a pure heart, O God, and renew a steadfast spirit within me" — corresponding to Keter, Chochmah, Binah, Da'at, Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet, and afterward "A song of ascents, I lift my eyes to the mountains" and the psalm "Hallelujah, praise God in His holiness" (according to the Rashash's prayerbook). It is written in Keter Malchut that it is proper to now say the verse "and the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun," etc. (and Rabbi Yosef Chaim found a correct reason for this, that it is the mystical secret of that verse within the intentions of the blessing of the moon).
takeaways: One says seven times "Create in me a pure heart" — corresponding to Keter, Chochmah, Binah, Da'at, Chesed, Gevurah, and Tiferet — followed by the Rashash's psalms.
It is proper to add the verse "and the light of the moon shall be as the light of the sun."

paragraphs: Omerim shelosh peamim "shalom alekem", uperashti bs"d hattaam bsh"q "mqbtzl" - deita bemidrash tanchuma (qedoshim tv): kisbaka asu al habberakot, yaredu meenayv shalosh demaot; hashshenayim yaredu, vehashshelishit niqshera ben enayv. ubazeh perashti bs"d hattaam denotenim hatztzedaqa bekol yom shene shelishim ushelish - lehagen miqqitrug shalosh demaot asher hashshenayim yaredu, vehashshelishit niqshera ben enayv; velazeh amar: "vehaya maaseh hatztzedaqa shalom", sheyyihyeh lanu shalom bah miqqitrug demaot esav shemmisseparo "shalom", velaken atta omerim shalosh peamim "shalom". gam perashti: kede leorer zekut yaaqob abinu "h sheshshemo kapul, veim hu male beva"v, missipro "shalom", vehu haya chay bechelqe nepesh rucha neshama shello, laken omerim shelosh peamim "shalom". ubazeh perashti: "vaamartem koh lechay"(shemuel  kh,v) - hu yaaqob shello met(taanit h:), "veatta shalom ubeteka shalom, vekol asher leka shalom".

clarification.explanation: One says "Shalom Aleichem" three times. Rabbi Yosef Chaim explains the reason (based on a midrash: when Esau wept over the blessings, three tears fell — two fell, and the third became lodged between his eyes). From this he also explained the custom of giving charity daily divided into two-thirds and one-third — corresponding to the two tears that fell and the one tear lodged between his eyes, in order to protect against the prosecution of those tears, as it is said, "and the work of righteousness shall be peace"; and likewise to arouse the merit of our father Jacob, whose name, when written fully with a vav and doubled (twice), equals "Shalom" (peace), and he lived at peace in every part of his soul — "and you shall be peace, and your house shall be peace."
takeaways: "Shalom Aleichem" is said three times at the conclusion of the blessing of the moon.
The custom of giving daily charity divided two-thirds and one-third corresponds to Esau's two fallen tears and the one lodged between his eyes, to guard against their prosecution.
The further reason: to arouse the merit of our father Jacob, whose full doubled name equals the numerical value of "Shalom."
